findings.title: AtomicFileWrite overwrite keeps the old file mode (0644 survives a 0o600 write), and no test exercises that path
findings.evidence: `_ = try FileManager.default.replaceItemAt(dest, withItemAt: tmp)`. By default replaceItemAt keeps the original item's metadata, permissions included. Checked with a scratch Swift probe: dest chmod 0644, tmp chmod 0600, after replaceItemAt the mode printed `644`. Every permission test writes a NEW file: AiTaskbarValidate/main.swift:798, UsageHistoryStoreTests.swift:27-33, ConfigLoaderSecretTests.swift:212-225.
findings.impact: Once a secret file exists with a loose mode, every later write(permissions:0o600) leaves it 0644. That breaks the 0o600-at-write-time rule, and the suite stays green.
findings.fix: Add a test that pre-creates dest at 0644. Use .usingNewMetadataOnly, rename(2), or an explicit final mode.
findings.cetico_evidence: Sources/AiTaskbarCore/Cache/AtomicFileWrite.swift:20-27: the temp file is chmod'd to the requested mode, then replaceItemAt(dest, withItemAt: tmp) swaps it in. replaceItemAt keeps the destination's old metadata, so write(permissions:0o600) does not deliver the mode it promises (doc comment lines 8-12) whenever the file already exists with a looser mode. Downgraded from HIGH: the app creates its secret files 0600 from the start, config.toml is re-chmodded on load, and app dirs are 0700 (the security panel's vote). A loose mode only gets there from outside the app, so this is a contract defect, not a reachable leak.

findings.title: The canPersistCredentials guard that stops rotation of a /usr/bin/security-fallback credential is never tested at provider level
findings.evidence: `if manageOAuthRefresh, credentialReader.canPersistCredentials, credentials.isExpired(...)`. MockKeychainReader (AnthropicProviderE2ETests.swift:10) inherits the default `{ true }` (AnthropicCredentialReading.swift:48). The only asserts on the flag are at reader level (SecurityToolCredentialReaderTests.swift:211,291).
findings.impact: Removing the guard passes the suite. The provider would then rotate the shared Claude Code refresh token without being able to write it back, which logs the CLI out.
findings.fix: Give the mock a canPersistCredentials property. Add an E2E test: expired token, manage=true, canPersist=false, asserting 0 refresh hits and an empty writeBackCalls.
findings.cetico_evidence: The guard exists at AnthropicProvider.swift:87-88. MockKeychainReader gets the protocol default canPersistCredentials {true} (AnthropicCredentialReading.swift:48). The only asserts on the flag are reader-level (SecurityToolCredentialReaderTests.swift:211,291), and the E2E refresh test (AnthropicProviderE2ETests.swift:191-221) runs with canPersist=true. Deleting the guard keeps the suite green. Downgraded: the defect is a missing test, not a bug. The code is correct today, and the path needs opt-in manage_oauth_refresh=true plus the security-tool fallback.

findings.title: The vacuous-#expect grep misses the Optional-Bool form when a message argument follows, and a live instance guards TLS pins
findings.evidence: The regex requires `)` right after the literal. Escape: Tests/AiTaskbarCoreTests/PinStoreTests.swift:319 `#expect(pin?.isEmpty == false, "empty baseline pin for \(host)")`. It also misses #require, `!= true/false` and multi-line asserts. The regex is duplicated in ci.yml:37 with no planted-form self-test.
findings.impact: An empty TLS pin may pass, and any assert with a message argument bypasses the gate.
findings.fix: Use expectFalse(pin?.isEmpty ?? true). Widen the regex, scan multi-line, share one script between validate.sh and CI, and add a self-test.
findings.cetico_evidence: The regex gap is real: scripts/validate.sh:118 and ci.yml:37 require ')' right after true/false, so `#expect(opt == false, "msg")` is not caught. But the live instance is NOT vacuous today. A scratch package on the current bundled Testing (Xcode.app) made `#expect(s?.isEmpty == false, "msg")`, `#expect(x == false)` with x:Bool?=true, and `#expect(false == true)` all FAIL correctly. The vacuity was a former-toolchain artifact (CLAUDE.md). The 'empty TLS pin may pass' impact is also refuted: PinStoreTests.swift:329 `#expect(pin.count == 44)` is a non-optional Int comparison and fails on an empty pin. Left: gate-hardening debt.

findings.title: coverage.sh stops enforcing the floor, and passes, when the floor is fractional
findings.evidence: `if [ "$FLOOR" -gt 0 ]` errors on 91.5. The error does not trigger set -e inside an if condition, so the else branch runs `warn no floor enforced` and exits 0. BELOW (line 53) is never read.
findings.impact: Raising the ratchet to a fractional value (the baseline is 91.53) disables the gate.
findings.fix: Compare with awk and reject a non-numeric FLOOR.
findings.cetico_evidence: scripts/coverage.sh:55 `[ "$FLOOR" -gt 0 ]` with FLOOR=91.5 prints 'integer expected', takes the else branch and exits 0 (reproduced under set -euo pipefail). The sub-claim 'BELOW is never read' is false: line 56 reads it. Downgraded: the script documents floor as an integer (line 7) and the active floor is 90, so the bug is latent.

findings.title: Error-mapping tests put their only assert inside if case, so a wrong error variant passes
findings.evidence: `if case .http(let status, _) = err { #expect(status == 503) }` has no else. Same at OAuthRefresherTests.swift:91,110 and FileCredentialReaderTests.swift:140,160.
findings.impact: A wrong AppError variant, e.g. 5xx mapped to .transport, passes all five tests. The back-off and the Authorize banner depend on these variants.
findings.fix: Use guard case ... else { Issue.record } or compare the whole AppError.
findings.cetico_evidence: FetchPayloadTests.swift:57-59, OAuthRefresherTests.swift:91,110 and FileCredentialReaderTests.swift:140,160 use `if case ... { #expect }` with no else, so a different AppError variant passes. Downgraded: this is a weak assert. No product bug is shown.

findings.title: RefreshScheduler 429 back-off is untested and its loop has no injectable clock
findings.evidence: The back-off branch with enter/exitRateLimitBackoff and Task.sleep(rateLimitBackoff) has 0 references to rateLimitBackoff in Tests. The App target is outside the coverage gate.
findings.impact: Removing or inverting the back-off goes undetected, and 429 vendors are polled at full cadence.
findings.fix: Inject a sleeper and assert sleeps [interval, 60] plus enter/exit order.
findings.cetico_evidence: RefreshScheduler.swift:93-104: the back-off branch has no test (0 refs to rateLimitBackoff/enterRateLimitBackoff in Tests), and the loop has no clock seam. Downgraded: the input flag hasRateLimitedVendor is well pinned (AggregatesComputationTests.swift:65-94), and the App target is outside the coverage gate by policy.

findings.title: RefreshSchedulerTests makes a real api.github.com request and depends on a 50 ms wall-clock window
findings.evidence: Line 16 uses the default HTTPClient (UpdateChecker.swift:66). Line 31 sleeps 50 ms, then line 33 expects status == .checking.
findings.impact: Flaky when offline or on a loaded runner, and it hits a real third-party endpoint.
findings.fix: Use a stubbed, blocking HTTPClient, mark the suite .serialized, and await the status instead of sleeping.
findings.cetico_evidence: RefreshSchedulerTests.swift:16 builds UpdateChecker without http:, so it gets the default HTTPClient() (UpdateChecker.swift:65) and makes a real request to api.github.com/repos/test/repo (UpdateChecker.swift:150). It then sleeps 50 ms (:31) and expects .checking (:33). Offline, the request fails fast, status leaves .checking and the test goes red. LOW: it only affects test determinism.

findings.title: The safe-by-default manageOAuthRefresh=false on provider inits is not pinned by any test
findings.evidence: The init defaults (AnthropicProvider.swift:28,38; OpenAIProvider.swift:38,49) are always overridden in tests.
findings.impact: Flipping a default to true passes the suite.
findings.fix: Add a default-init test with an expired token and 0 refresh hits.
findings.cetico_evidence: The claim 'always overridden in tests' is inaccurate: default-init tests exist (AnthropicProviderE2ETests.swift:112,279,310; OpenAIProviderE2ETests.swift:59,238). But all of them use non-expired tokens (e.g. :107, :277, :308), so flipping the default to true stays green. AppConfigTests.swift:19-20 pins only the config default.

findings.title: coverage.sh uses find | head -1 to pick profdata and the test binary
findings.evidence: PROFDATA and BINARY come from the first find match, not from the active bin path.
findings.cetico_evidence: coverage.sh:31-33 does use find | head -1. In this worktree only one candidate exists (.build/arm64-apple-macosx/debug/{codecov/default.profdata, ai-taskbarPackageTests.xctest}). A stale read needs a second test-build tree (e.g. x86_64), which was not observed.

findings.title: The warning allowlist accepts ANY deprecation in the Keychain files, not just the classic Keychain API
findings.evidence: The regex is `...\.swift:N:N: warning:.*was deprecated`, and the test only covers SecACL/SecKeychainCreate.
findings.impact: Unrelated deprecations in those files are allowlisted silently.
findings.fix: Restrict to SecKeychain/SecACL/SecTrustedApplication/kSecUseAuthenticationUI and add a negative case.
findings.cetico_evidence: This allowlist scope is a documented decision. CLAUDE.md section 5 says 'Only deprecations in Sources/.../Keychain{AccessAuthorizer,CredentialReader,PromptSuppressor}.swift and their isolated-keychain test fixtures ... are allowlisted. Other warnings in those files fail too', which is exactly the regex at check-swift-warnings.sh:11. Narrowing it is a hardening idea, not a defect.

findings.title: The CachedFetch cancellation test accepts AppError.other and depends on 50 ms timing
findings.evidence: `if case .other = err { return true }` plus a 50 ms sleep before cancel, with the stub blocking Thread.sleep(5).
findings.impact: An unrelated .other failure counts as observed cancellation.
findings.fix: Require CancellationError or URLError.cancelled, and release the stub with a semaphore.
findings.cetico_evidence: CachedFetchEdgeTests.swift:136 accepts .other. The 50 ms sleep is at :122, and the stub blocks 5 s (:110). The claimed 'green on decode error' is unproven: empty data maps to .schema, not .other. .other only comes from AppError wrapping a non-AppError (AppError.swift:67).

findings.title: DiskCache TTL/stale tests use the real clock, so the boundary semantics are not pinned
findings.evidence: ttl 0.001 plus Thread.sleep(0.05). Same at line 94. No clock seam.
findings.cetico_evidence: DiskCache.swift:78,87,102 use Date.now with no clock seam, and the `age <= ttl` boundary (:88) cannot be pinned. The tests use ttl 0.001 plus Thread.sleep(0.05) (DiskCacheTests.swift:26-28, 92-94), so a <= vs < mutation is not caught.

findings.title: The 3 known issues are intentional negative controls and hide no defect
findings.evidence: withKnownIssue wraps expectTrue(false), expectFalse(true) and expectTrue(absent ?? false) at lines 113, 116 and 120.
findings.cetico_evidence: There is no defect. The finding itself says these are intentional negative controls (TestingInfrastructureTests.swift:113-120, withKnownIssue). Close it.
